pathway.title: UWM Holdings Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. Leverage on the company's own capital measure more than doubled in six months. Non-funding debt (senior notes, servicing-rights lines, borrowings against investment securities and finance leases) rose by USD 1,747.5 million, from USD 4,292.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 6,040.4 million at June 30, 2026, while total equity fell by USD 608.3 million, from USD 1,593.6 million to USD 985.3 million, taking non-funding debt to equity from 2.69x to 6.13x [CP-1, Financials and credit metrics]. The increase was USD 1,750.0 million of net draws on the two servicing-rights facilities, which exceeded the USD 1,237.7 million growth in the servicing-rights asset, so part of the borrowing financed operations and distributions rather than the asset. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the use of proceeds.

2. Adjusted EBITDA and net income diverged sharply because of hedging. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months was USD 790.6 million, and non-funding debt was 7.64x that figure, against 6.16x at FY2025; yet the last twelve months produced a net loss of USD 105.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA excludes servicing-rights valuation changes and the result on other interest rate derivatives, which together were a net loss of USD 526.8 million over the last twelve months and USD 538.1 million in the second quarter alone. In the second quarter a derivative loss of USD 603.2 million was only partly offset by a USD 65.1 million servicing-rights valuation gain, so the hedge programme lost money net. The filings do not state the intended hedge ratio. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the hedge result.

3. Coverage of interest on non-funding debt is thinner than the headline Adjusted EBITDA suggests. Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA covers interest expense on non-funding debt 2.92x, down from 3.25x at FY2025, and the second-quarter run rate is lower still at 2.14x (Adjusted EBITDA of USD 185.9 million and interest of USD 86.8 million, each annualised). These are accrual proxies because cash interest on non-funding debt is not reported separately. Category: Analyst Interpretation on CP-1 figures.

4. Liquidity is adequate for the near term but depends on lender discretion. Cash of USD 477.4 million (unrestricted) plus USD 800.0 million of undrawn lines gives USD 1,277.4 million, of which USD 300.0 million sits under uncommitted servicing-rights facilities that advance against collateral value and may be curtailed if that value falls [Q2 10-Q page:54, page:55]. The USD 500.0 million revolver is provided by the controlling holder. Scheduled non-funding repayments are USD 83.7 million in the second half of 2026 and USD 2,375.0 million in 2027 (the 2027 notes of USD 500.0 million and the Conventional servicing-rights facility of USD 1,875.0 million). Without new money, 2027 repayments would be 185.9% of current headroom. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

5. Short-dated warehouse funding is the structural exposure beneath the debt. Warehouse lines of USD 8,600.1 million fund mortgage loans of USD 9,619.1 million, only USD 900.0 million of line capacity is committed, advances are generally 97% to 98% of principal, and lines with USD 5,090.8 million advanced have expiry dates on or before May 14, 2027. Every facility, including the secured and unsecured lines, carries cross-default or cross-acceleration provisions, so a covenant breach or an unmet margin call under one could terminate all of them [Q2 10-Q page:50, page:52]. The company states compliance with all covenants at June 30, 2026, and no covenant levels are printed. Category: Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on covenant headroom.

6. Controlling-holder structure cuts both ways. SFS Corp. holds 78.7% of Holdings LLC and about 79% of votes, receives member distributions and Tax Receivable Agreement payments (liability USD 280.0 million, accelerating on a change in control), and also subordinated its USD 500.0 million revolver to the senior notes in September 2025 and took part in the August 2026 preferred issue through a vehicle of the CEO's family [CP-1A, Ownership and control; Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Distributions and dividends paid in the first half of 2026 were USD 321.8 million against a net loss of USD 281.5 million before the dividend was suspended. Behaviour reads as mixed. Category: Analyst Interpretation on documented actions.

7. The August 5, 2026 raise improves the equity position but its effect cannot yet be measured. The USD 1,650.0 million of gross proceeds has not reached any reported statement, its use of proceeds, fees and balance sheet classification are not supplied, and the contingent rights offering of USD 400 million is scheduled to expire after the cutoff. If the proceeds were retained or used to repay secured lines and were classified as equity, non-funding debt to equity would be between 2.29x and 1.67x; if the preferred is classified outside equity and proceeds repay secured lines, it would be 4.46x. These are arithmetic scenarios, not forecasts. Annual dividends at the stated rates would be USD 165.0 million in cash or USD 214.5 million non-cash. Category: Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information on terms.

8. Regulatory net worth and liquidity floors are close enough to matter. The most restrictive agency minimums are net worth of USD 743.6 million and liquidity of USD 343.9 million for UWM, against consolidated total equity of USD 985.3 million and unrestricted cash of USD 477.4 million at June 30, 2026 [Q2 10-Q page:23]. Consolidated equity includes non-controlling interest and is not UWM's own net worth, which is not printed, so the USD 241.7 million gap is a proxy only. A second-quarter-sized fall in equity (USD 615.6 million) would have exceeded that proxy gap before the August raise. Category: Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information on UWM-level figures.

runs.text: - Agency-eligible, high-volume origination. About 93% of loans in the second quarter of 2026 went to Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae pools, and originations were USD 84,646.4 million for the first half of 2026, 17.4% above the first half of 2025, so most production has an agency exit and the lines turn over within a month [CP-1A, Company and operating model; CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact. - Servicing-rights asset and earnings drivers. Servicing income rose to USD 220.5 million in the second quarter from USD 178.8 million a year earlier, and the servicing-rights asset of USD 5,311.5 million is 2.14% of USD 247.6 billion serviced; it supports secured borrowing and can be sold, with USD 801.0 million of net sale proceeds in the first half [CP-1, Earnings, cash flow and servicing drivers]. Category: Documentary Fact. - Fresh junior capital and owner participation. The August 2026 preferred and warrant issue of USD 1,650.0 million included USD 150.0 million from a vehicle of the CEO's family, the dividend was suspended, and the owner's revolver is subordinated to the senior notes [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on creditor benefit. - Spread maturity profile on senior notes. The four note series mature in 2027, 2029, 2030 and 2031 (USD 500.0 million, 700.0 million, 800.0 million and 1,000.0 million), with none in 2028, and the 2027 notes are callable at par [CP-1, Chart data: debt maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact. - Reported covenant compliance. The company states compliance with indenture and facility covenants at June 30, 2026, and the tests that are printed for note incurrence (Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio of at least 3.0 to 1.0 or Debt-to-Equity Ratio not above 2.0 to 1.0) restrict new non-funding debt [Q2 10-Q page:54]. Category: Documentary Fact; the restriction's effect is Analyst Interpretation.

- High and rising leverage on thin equity. Non-funding debt to equity of 6.13x and 7.64x LTM Adjusted EBITDA; equity ex non-controlling interest is only USD 133.8 million [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact. - Earnings volatility and hedge losses. Net loss of USD 451.9 million in the second quarter after a USD 603.2 million derivative loss; recurring servicing-rights decay of USD 395.1 million in the first half is not added back in Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1, Adjusted EBITDA definition and reconciliation review]. Category: Documentary Fact. - Negative operating cash flow. Operating cash flow was negative USD 1,885.8 million for the first half of 2026, and negative USD 1,084.8 million after adding servicing-rights sale proceeds, against positive USD 1,919.8 million a year earlier on the same basis; secured borrowing of USD 1,750.0 million plugged the gap [CP-1, Calculations]. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on funding the gap. - Uncommitted and short-dated funding with cross-default. Only USD 900.0 million of warehouse line capacity is committed, the servicing-rights facilities are uncommitted and collateral-based, and cross-default links all lines [Q2 10-Q page:15, page:52]. Category: Documentary Fact. - Controlling-holder claims and related-party flows. Tax Receivable Agreement liability of USD 280.0 million, member distributions of USD 261.9 million paid in the first half of 2026, and related-party payments of USD 32.9 million in FY2025 [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour; Claims outside debt in CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact. - Execution and legal risks. The in-house servicing transition (management targets October 2026) and class actions on broker influence, telemarketing and a vendor cyber incident; no accrual or estimate is printed [CP-1A, Timeline; Credit translations]. Category: Management Language for the timeline; Documentary Fact for the proceedings. - Terms of the August 2026 raise are unknown. Redemption and protective rights of the Series A-1 preferred and the board rights of Oaktree could rank ahead of creditor interests in practice. The filing does not say. Category: Insufficient Information.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On August 5, 2026 UWMC closed a "strategic capital transaction" with affiliates of Oaktree Capital Management and entities affiliated with its Chairman, President and CEO, with gross proceeds of 1.65 billion (Q2 10-Q page:32). Oaktree invested 1.5 billion for 1.5 million shares of Series A-1 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 150 million Class A shares at 2.00 per share and over 150 million at 6.00 per share. SFS Group Capital, LLC invested 150.0 million for 150,000 shares of Series A-2 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 15 million shares at 2.00 and over 15 million at 6.00. Both series have an original issue price of 1,000 per share and accrue cumulative dividends of 10.0% per annum when paid in cash or 13.0% per annum when not paid in cash and added to stated value. Series A-2 is subordinate to Series A-1 in certain circumstances and has no governance protections. The certificate of designation includes redemption, governance and investor-protection rights for Series A-1 holders that the note does not describe, and an investor rights agreement lets Oaktree appoint two directors, one of them independent. In connection with the issue the company announced its intention to launch a 400 million rights offering to Class A holders "if needed", with the support of Oaktree and the Ishbia family, at a price equal to the greater of 2.00 and 85% of a ten-day volume-weighted average price, for up to 200 million Class A shares, with a record date of October 2, 2026 and expiry on November 12, 2026 (page:33). The filing states the effects are not reflected in the financial statements. The Q2 release headline calls the transaction a "$2.05 Billion Equity Investment"; the filing treats the 1.65 billion as closed and the 400 million as contingent, and the two are logged as a conflict below. Use of proceeds, issuance costs, balance sheet classification (equity or mezzanine), the redemption terms and the financing effect on the servicing-rights facilities are Insufficient Information. This is an equity-type transaction; it adds no new debt.

New debt issues in the period covered: the most recent senior note issue was the 1.0 billion 6.250% senior notes due March 15, 2031 issued on September 9, 2025 by Holdings LLC and guaranteed by UWM; its proceeds were used to repay the 800.0 million 2025 senior notes at maturity, temporarily pay down servicing-rights facilities and for working capital (Q2 10-Q page:17 to page:18, page:53). Before that, 800.0 million of 6.625% notes due February 1, 2030 were issued by Holdings LLC on December 10, 2024. No senior notes were issued in the first half of 2026 (cash flow statement page:5). Debt capacity rose through facility changes: the Ginnie Mae servicing-rights facility was amended in March 2026 to 900.0 million of uncommitted capacity with later maturity, and by June 30, 2026 the two servicing-rights facilities show limits of 2.0 billion and 1.25 billion (Q1 10-Q page:16; Q2 10-Q page:15 to page:16); the amendment that raised those limits in the second quarter is not described. Drawn balances on the servicing-rights lines were 2,950.0 million at June 30, 2026 against 1,200.0 million at December 31, 2025 (CP-1).

The terminated Two Harbors transaction: under the Merger Agreement dated December 17, 2025, Two Harbors common stockholders would receive 2.3328 UWMC Class A shares per share, and each series of Two Harbors preferred stock would convert into a like UWMC preferred series (8.125% Series A, 7.625% Series B and 7.25% Series C), with closing expected in the second quarter of 2026 (10-K page:140). The 10-K expected about 247 million Class A shares to be issued (page:74). The deck described the transaction as adding servicing UPB and being accretive and "de-levering" (management claims, deck page:7). The agreement was later terminated, with a fee received in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:37), and second-quarter general and administrative expense included costs "related to the terminated merger agreement" (Q2 10-Q page:46). Termination date, payer, fee amount and reason are Insufficient Information.

The company's own leverage measure is non-funding debt to total equity, which was 6.13x at June 30, 2026 against 2.69x at December 31, 2025, because debt rose by 1,747.5 million while total equity fell by 608.3 million to 985.3 million. On Adjusted EBITDA, which already deducts warehouse interest but not interest on non-funding debt, non-funding debt was 7.64x the last twelve months at June 30, 2026 (790.6 million), against 6.16x at FY2025 (697.3 million). Earnings quality is the central issue: Adjusted EBITDA for Q2 2026 was 185.9 million while the net loss was 451.9 million, because the company adds back a 603.2 million loss on other interest rate derivatives and removes a 65.1 million servicing-rights valuation gain. For the last twelve months those two excluded items net to a 526.8 million loss, and net loss was 105.0 million. Operating cash flow was negative 1,885.8 million for H1 2026, with servicing-rights sale proceeds of 801.0 million in investing activities, and the gap was funded by 1,750.0 million of net borrowing on the servicing-rights lines. Liquidity on the company's basis is about 1.3 billion (1,298.4 million with restricted cash), but 300.0 million of the undrawn lines is uncommitted and the 500.0 million revolver is provided by SFS Corp., an entity controlled by the CEO. Cash of 321.8 million was paid to equity holders in H1 2026 through dividends and member distributions. Warehouse lines with 5,090.8 million advanced expire on or before May 14, 2027, and 2,375.0 million of non-funding debt (the 2027 notes and the Conventional servicing-rights facility) falls due in 2027. All figures are unaudited for 2026 and exclude the August 5, 2026 preferred stock and warrant transaction, which closed after the period.

Weighted average discount rate fell to 8.9% from 9.4% and weighted average prepayment speed to 8.6% from 10.3% (`page:13`). fields.value: UWM Holdings Corp is the listed top holding company of a wholesale-only residential mortgage lender, so its creditors are exposed to one volume-driven business that earns through gain on sale, a retained servicing portfolio and net interest, and that is controlled by a single holder. The operating subsidiary originates only through independent mortgage brokers, sells about 93% of loans into Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae pools, and keeps the servicing rights on most of them, which is why the servicing-rights asset of 5,311.5 million and the borrowings against it dominate the funding story. Control rests with SFS Corp., an entity controlled by the CEO: it holds 78.7% of the economic units of Holdings LLC and, as the 10-K states, about 79% of voting power, and it is also the lender under the unsecured revolver, the counterparty to the Tax Receivable Agreement, and the recipient of member distributions. The decisive recent changes are two. First, the planned acquisition of Two Harbors Investment Corp., signed on December 17, 2025 and described in the 10-K as expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, was terminated in the first quarter of 2026 with a termination fee received, so the share issuance of roughly 247 million Class A shares and the added servicing portfolio did not occur. Second, on August 5, 2026, after a second quarter in which derivative losses drove a net loss of 451.9 million, the company closed a 1.65 billion preferred stock and warrant issue to Oaktree and a vehicle of the CEO's family, suspended the quarterly dividend, and announced a contingent 400 million rights offering. These actions add junior capital beneath the debt, but the filings supplied describe the preferred terms only in summary, and the effects are not in any reported financial statement. A creditor should therefore treat the capital raise as a material, documented positive for liquidity and loss absorption whose strength depends on terms that are not in the pack, while keeping the controlled-company structure, related-party flows and the in-house servicing transition as the main governance and execution uncertainties.

fields.value: On August 5, 2026 UWMC closed a "strategic capital transaction" with affiliates of Oaktree Capital Management and entities affiliated with its Chairman, President and CEO, with gross proceeds of 1.65 billion (Q2 10-Q `page:32`). Oaktree invested 1.5 billion for 1.5 million shares of Series A-1 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 150 million Class A shares at 2.00 per share and over 150 million at 6.00 per share. SFS Group Capital, LLC invested 150.0 million for 150,000 shares of Series A-2 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 15 million shares at 2.00 and over 15 million at 6.00. Both series have an original issue price of 1,000 per share and accrue cumulative dividends of 10.0% per annum when paid in cash or 13.0% per annum when not paid in cash and added to stated value. Series A-2 is subordinate to Series A-1 in certain circumstances and has no governance protections. The certificate of designation includes redemption, governance and investor-protection rights for Series A-1 holders that the note does not describe, and an investor rights agreement lets Oaktree appoint two directors, one of them independent. In connection with the issue the company announced its intention to launch a 400 million rights offering to Class A holders "if needed", with the support of Oaktree and the Ishbia family, at a price equal to the greater of 2.00 and 85% of a ten-day volume-weighted average price, for up to 200 million Class A shares, with a record date of October 2, 2026 and expiry on November 12, 2026 (`page:33`). The filing states the effects are not reflected in the financial statements. The Q2 release headline calls the transaction a "$2.05 Billion Equity Investment"; the filing treats the 1.65 billion as closed and the 400 million as contingent, and the two are logged as a conflict below. Use of proceeds, issuance costs, balance sheet classification (equity or mezzanine), the redemption terms and the financing effect on the servicing-rights facilities are Insufficient Information. This is an equity-type transaction; it adds no new debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This credit synthesis covers UWM Holdings Corp (UWMC) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway, using filings through the Form 10-Q signed August 7, 2026. It combines the accepted financial base and the accepted business and transaction context into a fundamental credit view for the debt of UWM and Holdings LLC. It gives no relative value, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Locators in brackets or tables are `page:N` of the pinned `.jsonl` text; "Q2 10-Q" is the Form 10-Q for June 30, 2026. Every CP-1 and CP-1A figure used below was re-checked against the filings while writing this answer. This answer confirms CP-1 and CP-1A and corrects neither.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: UWM Holdings Corp is a large, agency-focused mortgage originator whose credit position weakened in the first half of 2026 but was cushioned by new capital on August 5, 2026. The strongest support is the USD 1,650.0 million preferred issue, together with scale in agency-eligible origination and a USD 5,311.5 million servicing-rights asset. The weakest point is the balance sheet: non-funding debt of USD 6,040.4 million is 6.13x total equity of USD 985.3 million, and equity fell USD 615.6 million in the second quarter, mostly from a net loss driven by derivative losses. What decides the outcome is whether the preferred terms leave creditors protected, whether the uncommitted servicing-rights lines stay available into USD 2,375.0 million of 2027 maturities, and whether hedging losses stop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Leverage on the company's own capital measure more than doubled in six months. Non-funding debt (senior notes, servicing-rights lines, borrowings against investment securities and finance leases) rose by USD 1,747.5 million, from USD 4,292.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 6,040.4 million at June 30, 2026, while total equity fell by USD 608.3 million, from USD 1,593.6 million to USD 985.3 million, taking non-funding debt to equity from 2.69x to 6.13x [CP-1, Financials and credit metrics]. The increase was USD 1,750.0 million of net draws on the two servicing-rights facilities, which exceeded the USD 1,237.7 million growth in the servicing-rights asset, so part of the borrowing financed operations and distributions rather than the asset. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the use of proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Adjusted EBITDA and net income diverged sharply because of hedging. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months was USD 790.6 million, and non-funding debt was 7.64x that figure, against 6.16x at FY2025; yet the last twelve months produced a net loss of USD 105.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA excludes servicing-rights valuation changes and the result on other interest rate derivatives, which together were a net loss of USD 526.8 million over the last twelve months and USD 538.1 million in the second quarter alone. In the second quarter a derivative loss of USD 603.2 million was only partly offset by a USD 65.1 million servicing-rights valuation gain, so the hedge programme lost money net. The filings do not state the intended hedge ratio. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the hedge result.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Coverage of interest on non-funding debt is thinner than the headline Adjusted EBITDA suggests. Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA covers interest expense on non-funding debt 2.92x, down from 3.25x at FY2025, and the second-quarter run rate is lower still at 2.14x (Adjusted EBITDA of USD 185.9 million and interest of USD 86.8 million, each annualised). These are accrual proxies because cash interest on non-funding debt is not reported separately. Category: Analyst Interpretation on CP-1 figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Liquidity is adequate for the near term but depends on lender discretion. Cash of USD 477.4 million (unrestricted) plus USD 800.0 million of undrawn lines gives USD 1,277.4 million, of which USD 300.0 million sits under uncommitted servicing-rights facilities that advance against collateral value and may be curtailed if that value falls [Q2 10-Q `page:54`, `page:55`]. The USD 500.0 million revolver is provided by the controlling holder. Scheduled non-funding repayments are USD 83.7 million in the second half of 2026 and USD 2,375.0 million in 2027 (the 2027 notes of USD 500.0 million and the Conventional servicing-rights facility of USD 1,875.0 million). Without new money, 2027 repayments would be 185.9% of current headroom. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Short-dated warehouse funding is the structural exposure beneath the debt. Warehouse lines of USD 8,600.1 million fund mortgage loans of USD 9,619.1 million, only USD 900.0 million of line capacity is committed, advances are generally 97% to 98% of principal, and lines with USD 5,090.8 million advanced have expiry dates on or before May 14, 2027. Every facility, including the secured and unsecured lines, carries cross-default or cross-acceleration provisions, so a covenant breach or an unmet margin call under one could terminate all of them [Q2 10-Q `page:50`, `page:52`]. The company states compliance with all covenants at June 30, 2026, and no covenant levels are printed. Category: Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Controlling-holder structure cuts both ways. SFS Corp. holds 78.7% of Holdings LLC and about 79% of votes, receives member distributions and Tax Receivable Agreement payments (liability USD 280.0 million, accelerating on a change in control), and also subordinated its USD 500.0 million revolver to the senior notes in September 2025 and took part in the August 2026 preferred issue through a vehicle of the CEO's family [CP-1A, Ownership and control; Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Distributions and dividends paid in the first half of 2026 were USD 321.8 million against a net loss of USD 281.5 million before the dividend was suspended. Behaviour reads as mixed. Category: Analyst Interpretation on documented actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. The August 5, 2026 raise improves the equity position but its effect cannot yet be measured. The USD 1,650.0 million of gross proceeds has not reached any reported statement, its use of proceeds, fees and balance sheet classification are not supplied, and the contingent rights offering of USD 400 million is scheduled to expire after the cutoff. If the proceeds were retained or used to repay secured lines and were classified as equity, non-funding debt to equity would be between 2.29x and 1.67x; if the preferred is classified outside equity and proceeds repay secured lines, it would be 4.46x. These are arithmetic scenarios, not forecasts. Annual dividends at the stated rates would be USD 165.0 million in cash or USD 214.5 million non-cash. Category: Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information on terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Regulatory net worth and liquidity floors are close enough to matter. The most restrictive agency minimums are net worth of USD 743.6 million and liquidity of USD 343.9 million for UWM, against consolidated total equity of USD 985.3 million and unrestricted cash of USD 477.4 million at June 30, 2026 [Q2 10-Q `page:23`]. Consolidated equity includes non-controlling interest and is not UWM's own net worth, which is not printed, so the USD 241.7 million gap is a proxy only. A second-quarter-sized fall in equity (USD 615.6 million) would have exceeded that proxy gap before the August raise. Category: Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information on UWM-level figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Agency-eligible, high-volume origination. About 93% of loans in the second quarter of 2026 went to Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae pools, and originations were USD 84,646.4 million for the first half of 2026, 17.4% above the first half of 2025, so most production has an agency exit and the lines turn over within a month [CP-1A, Company and operating model; CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Servicing-rights asset and earnings drivers. Servicing income rose to USD 220.5 million in the second quarter from USD 178.8 million a year earlier, and the servicing-rights asset of USD 5,311.5 million is 2.14% of USD 247.6 billion serviced; it supports secured borrowing and can be sold, with USD 801.0 million of net sale proceeds in the first half [CP-1, Earnings, cash flow and servicing drivers]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fresh junior capital and owner participation. The August 2026 preferred and warrant issue of USD 1,650.0 million included USD 150.0 million from a vehicle of the CEO's family, the dividend was suspended, and the owner's revolver is subordinated to the senior notes [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on creditor benefit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Spread maturity profile on senior notes. The four note series mature in 2027, 2029, 2030 and 2031 (USD 500.0 million, 700.0 million, 800.0 million and 1,000.0 million), with none in 2028, and the 2027 notes are callable at par [CP-1, Chart data: debt maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported covenant compliance. The company states compliance with indenture and facility covenants at June 30, 2026, and the tests that are printed for note incurrence (Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio of at least 3.0 to 1.0 or Debt-to-Equity Ratio not above 2.0 to 1.0) restrict new non-funding debt [Q2 10-Q `page:54`]. Category: Documentary Fact; the restriction's effect is Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High and rising leverage on thin equity. Non-funding debt to equity of 6.13x and 7.64x LTM Adjusted EBITDA; equity ex non-controlling interest is only USD 133.8 million [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings volatility and hedge losses. Net loss of USD 451.9 million in the second quarter after a USD 603.2 million derivative loss; recurring servicing-rights decay of USD 395.1 million in the first half is not added back in Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1, Adjusted EBITDA definition and reconciliation review]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Negative operating cash flow. Operating cash flow was negative USD 1,885.8 million for the first half of 2026, and negative USD 1,084.8 million after adding servicing-rights sale proceeds, against positive USD 1,919.8 million a year earlier on the same basis; secured borrowing of USD 1,750.0 million plugged the gap [CP-1, Calculations]. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on funding the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Uncommitted and short-dated funding with cross-default. Only USD 900.0 million of warehouse line capacity is committed, the servicing-rights facilities are uncommitted and collateral-based, and cross-default links all lines [Q2 10-Q `page:15`, `page:52`]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Controlling-holder claims and related-party flows. Tax Receivable Agreement liability of USD 280.0 million, member distributions of USD 261.9 million paid in the first half of 2026, and related-party payments of USD 32.9 million in FY2025 [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour; Claims outside debt in CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Execution and legal risks. The in-house servicing transition (management targets October 2026) and class actions on broker influence, telemarketing and a vendor cyber incident; no accrual or estimate is printed [CP-1A, Timeline; Credit translations]. Category: Management Language for the timeline; Documentary Fact for the proceedings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Terms of the August 2026 raise are unknown. Redemption and protective rights of the Series A-1 preferred and the board rights of Oaktree could rank ahead of creditor interests in practice. The filing does not say. Category: Insufficient Information.

fields.value: - Improvement: the certificate of designation shows no holder redemption right ahead of debt maturities; use of proceeds repays secured lines; hedge losses stop and equity rebuilds; the 2027 notes and the Conventional facility are extended; uncommitted capacity is replaced by committed lines.
